2026-12-24.title: 24 December · Advent Weekday (Morning Mass)
readings: The kingdom of David shall endure forever before the Lord
For ever I will sing the goodness of the Lord
The dawn from on high will break upon us
2026-12-24.alt: Morning Mass of 24 December. In the evening the Vigil Mass of Christmas is celebrated (Isaiah 62:1–5; Acts 13:16–17, 22–25; Matthew 1:1–25).
2026-12-24.verse: By the tender mercy of our God, the dawn from on high will break upon us, to give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.
theo: On the last morning of Advent the Church sings with Zechariah. Filled with the Holy Spirit, the old priest who had been silent for nine months bursts into the Benedictus, the song the Church prays every morning at Lauds. He blesses God who “has looked favorably on his people and redeemed them” and has “raised up a mighty savior for us in the house of his servant David”, the promise of 2 Samuel 7 now fulfilled.

Then he turns to his own child: “And you, child, will be called the prophet of the Most High; for you will go before the Lord to prepare his ways.” And the song ends with the image of dawn: “the dawn from on high will break upon us, to give light to those who sit in darkness.” Tonight that dawn breaks. Advent ends not with a lecture but with a song of praise and a sunrise.
outline: Ask: how will you greet Christmas: with hurry or with praise?
Point 1 · A mighty saviour from David's house
Point 2 · Prophet of the Most High
John prepares the way; so do we.
Point 3 · The dawn from on high
“To guide our feet into the way of peace.”
live: Make one act of peace in the family before Midnight Mass.
2026-12-24.prayer: Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel; he has visited his people and redeemed them. Let the dawn from on high break upon our home tonight, give light to those in darkness, and guide our feet into the way of peace. Amen.
altar: This is the last Mass of Advent. Tonight the same altar will receive the One born in Bethlehem, the house of bread.

quick: God raised up a mighty saviour from David's house.
John goes before the Lord to prepare his ways.
Tonight the dawn from on high breaks upon us.
2026-12-24.action: Make one act of peace in your family before Christmas night.
2026-12-24.question: Is my heart ready for the dawn of Christmas?

family.explain: Zechariah sang that God keeps his promises. Tonight Jesus comes like the morning sun to light up our darkness.
family.intention: We pray for families travelling and preparing for Christmas.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we keep a quiet moment for Jesus in today's busyness?”

pm.open: Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who has visited and redeemed his people. On this Christmas Eve, Lord, quiet our hearts and prepare us for your coming. Amen.
share: God kept his promise to David (2 Samuel 7:16). How has God kept his promises to me?
Zechariah sings of serving God without fear (Luke 1:74). What fear keeps me from serving God?
How will I keep a moment of silence today?
pm.resp: Blessed be the Lord, who has visited his people.
interc: For the Church on this holy eve, that she may welcome Christ with faith.
For families gathering tonight, that they may be united in love.
For those alone, sick or grieving on Christmas Eve.
For peace in the Holy Land and wherever there is war.
For our group, that we may serve God without fear.
pm.close: Lord God, by your tender mercy the dawn from on high breaks upon us. Guide our feet into the way of peace, and prepare us to welcome your Son tonight. Amen.

illus: A mother in Thrissur, rushing on Christmas Eve, stopped at noon, sat with her children in front of the empty crib and read the Benedictus. Her son, now a priest, says that moment of silence was his best Christmas memory.

homily: Dear friends, this morning Mass on Christmas Eve is the last Mass of Advent. The first reading recalls God's promise to David: when your days are fulfilled, I will raise up your offspring after you, and I will establish his kingdom. I will be a father to him, and he shall be a son to me. Your throne shall be established for ever (2 Samuel 7:12–16).

In the Gospel Zechariah, filled with the Holy Spirit, sings the Benedictus: blessed be the Lord God of Israel, for he has looked favourably on his people and redeemed them. He has raised up a mighty saviour for us in the house of his servant David (Luke 1:68–69).
The Church sings this song every morning at Lauds. Today it has special meaning. The promise to David is about to be fulfilled tonight in Bethlehem, the city of David.

Zechariah sings that we are saved so that we might serve him without fear, in holiness and righteousness before him all our days (Luke 1:74–75). Christmas is not only a feast to enjoy; it is a call to holiness, a life of serving God without fear.

He ends: by the tender mercy of our God, the dawn from on high will break upon us, to give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace (Luke 1:78–79). Tonight the dawn breaks.

In the busyness of this day, cooking, cleaning, shopping, travelling, let us keep a moment of quiet. Let us pray the Benedictus, thank God for his faithfulness, and prepare our hearts for the Child who comes tonight. Amen.
kids: Children, tonight Jesus comes like the sunrise after a long night. Get your heart ready with a prayer!

intro: Zechariah's Benedictus: God keeps his promise, John prepares the way, and the dawn breaks tonight.

sub: God visits and redeems his people.
q: When your days are fulfilled and you lie down with your ancestors, I will raise up your offspring after you, who shall come forth from your body, and I will establish his kingdom.
Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, for he has looked favorably on his people and redeemed them. He has raised up a mighty savior for us in the house of his servant David.

sub: Forgiveness of sins prepares the heart.
q: A voice cries out: “In the wilderness prepare the way of the LORD, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.”
And you, child, will be called the prophet of the Most High; for you will go before the Lord to prepare his ways, to give knowledge of salvation to his people by the forgiveness of their sins.

sub: People in darkness see a great light.
He guides our feet into peace.
q: But for you who revere my name the sun of righteousness shall rise, with healing in its wings. You shall go out leaping like calves from the stall.
By the tender mercy of our God, the dawn from on high will break upon us, to give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.
points.apply: Make one act of peace in your family today.

concl: The dawn is breaking: Christ is near.
